questions.question: How does ISO 14644-1:2015 handle the limit for particles ≥5 µm in an ISO Class 5 cleanroom?

options.A: It directly adopts the value in the ≥5 µm column of Table 1 for ISO Class 5 as the formal basis of classification for that class
options.B: It is expressed separately with an M descriptor (such as ISO M (29; ≥ 5 µm); LSAPC), and cannot be used to define the ISO Class
options.C: It is replaced by the ≥5 µm limit of ISO Class 6, because ISO Class 5 classification does not apply to this particle size range
options.D: Particles ≥5 µm need not be controlled, because classification considers only ultrafine particle concentrations below 0.1 µm

questions.explanation: Classification considers only cumulative particles from 0.1 to 5 µm; to correspond to the ≥5 µm requirement in the EU, PIC/S, and WHO sterile product annexes, the ≥5 µm limit for ISO Class 5 is expressed as an M descriptor. An M descriptor may be cited alone or alongside the ISO Class, but cannot be used to define the ISO Class.
questions.reference: ISO 14644-1:2015 §4.3, Table 1 note f; §3.2.6; Annex C §C.7

questions.question: According to ISO 14644-1 Table 1, what is the maximum permitted concentration for ISO Class 5 at ≥0.5 µm?
questions.explanation: ISO Class 5 at ≥0.5 µm is 3,520 particles/m³, which can be calculated from the formula Cn = 10^N × (0.1/D)^2.08. The value 352,000 is ISO Class 7 and 3,520,000 is ISO Class 8, which are easily confused because they differ by only one or two orders of magnitude.

questions.question: An ISO Class 5 cleanroom is classified at ≥0.5 µm, and Annex A gives a minimum single sample volume Vs of about 5.68 L per location. If the particle counter flow rate is 28.3 L/min, how should each sampling location be sampled?

options.A: Sample for 1 minute (28.3 L), because the minimum sampling time per location is 1 minute
options.B: Sample only 5.68 L, about 12 seconds, because the minimum sample volume from the formula has been reached
options.C: Sample for 20 minutes, because the detection target is 20 particles and sampling must run until enough time has accumulated
options.D: Adjust the sample volume according to the particle count at each location, and shorten sampling at locations with fewer particles to save testing time

questions.explanation: Annex A requires the sample volume at each location to be sufficient to detect at least 20 particles if the concentration were exactly at the limit, with a minimum of 2 L and a minimum of 1 minute, and the single sample volume must be the same at every location. So although 5.68 L satisfies the formula, sampling must still be 1 minute (28.3 L).

questions.question: Classification under ISO 14644-1 can be performed in three occupancy states. Which correctly describes the at-rest state?

options.A: The facility is complete with services connected and functioning, but with no production equipment, materials, or personnel present
options.B: The facility is functioning in the specified manner, with the specified number of personnel working in the agreed manner
options.C: The equipment has not yet been installed, and only the building space and HVAC system are complete and running
options.D: The equipment is installed and operating in the agreed manner, but with no personnel present

questions.explanation: At-rest means the equipment is installed and operating but no personnel are present. "The facility is complete with services connected, but with no production equipment, materials, or personnel" describes as-built, and "the specified number of personnel working in the agreed manner" describes operational. The occupancy state used must be stated for classification.

questions.question: During classification testing, the particle count at one sampling location exceeds the limit, and investigation confirms the cause is a technical fault in cleanroom equipment. According to Annex A, which handling is correct?

options.A: Treat the data as an aberrant event and discard it, note it in the report, and resample once directly
options.B: After the cause is identified and corrected, retest the failed location, adjacent locations, and other affected locations
options.C: As long as the overall average of all sampling locations does not exceed the limit, the room can be judged to pass
options.D: Exclude that location, and use the average of the remaining locations as the final basis of judgment

questions.explanation: An excursion caused by a technical fault requires the cause to be identified and corrected, and the failed location, surrounding locations, and other affected locations to be retested. Only an excursion caused by an "identified aberrant event" may be discarded, noted in the report, and resampled, and "treat the data as an aberrant event and discard it" is exactly this trap. Under §A.6.2.1, the average at every sampling location must meet the limit, and the overall average cannot be used to mask it.

questions.question: The scope of ISO 14644-5 covers many aspects of cleanroom operations. Which of the following is NOT something it specifies in detail?

options.A: Selection, change frequency, and laundering of cleanroom garments
options.B: Personnel training content and ongoing monitoring of compliance
options.C: Detailed sampling methods for routine particle and microbial monitoring programs
options.D: Maintaining cleanroom cleanliness through systematic cleaning procedures and frequencies

questions.explanation: Part 5 covers the operational procedure system, garments, personnel training, fixed equipment, materials and portable equipment, cleaning, and so on. Routine monitoring methods are not within its detailed scope, and reference should be made to ISO 14644-2 and 14644-3 for particle monitoring and to ISO 14698-1 and 14698-2 for microbial monitoring.

questions.question: According to ISO 14644-5, under which circumstance may cleanroom garments (whether packaged clean garments or used soiled garments) leave the storage area and the cleanroom?

options.A: An employee changes out of them before leaving work for comfort, wears them home, and brings them back
options.B: As long as they are fully packaged, they may be carried freely in any corridor of the plant
options.C: As long as the garments pass a visual inspection with no damage, they may be taken out
options.D: Only for the purpose of laundering, repair, or replacement

questions.explanation: §4.2.7 specifies that cleanroom garments must not be taken out of the storage area and cleanroom unless for laundering, repair, or replacement. The purpose is to prevent the garments from being contaminated in the outside environment and to avoid bringing outside contamination back in.

questions.question: How does ISO 14644-5 require the preventive maintenance (PM) schedule for fixed equipment to be set?

options.A: Components are renewed or replaced in time, before they become sources of contamination
options.B: Repair is done after the equipment fails or generates abnormal particles, to reduce the number of startups and shutdowns
options.C: It matches the cleanroom classification frequency, once a year being sufficient
options.D: It follows the procurement cycle of components, to reduce spare parts inventory cost

questions.explanation: §4.4.6 requires the PM schedule to be arranged so that components are renewed or replaced before they become sources of contamination. Waiting until failure is corrective maintenance, by which time a contamination risk has already arisen.

questions.question: In the terminology of ISO 14644-5, how does a fibre differ from an ordinary particle?

options.A: A fibre is a particle larger than 5 µm in diameter, distinguished from other particles by a size threshold
options.B: A fibre is a particle with an aspect ratio of 10 or more
options.C: A fibre is a particle shed only from cleanroom garment material, distinguished by its source
options.D: A fibre is a particle with microbial activity that can multiply in the environment, distinguished by its activity

questions.explanation: Part 5 defines a fibre as a particle with an aspect ratio of 10 or more. The definition has nothing to do with particle size, source, or whether it carries microorganisms, so "larger than 5 µm", "shed only from garments", and "microbially active" are not the basis of the definition.

questions.question: Cleaning staff are preparing to clean an area that still contains work-in-process. According to ISO 14644-5, how should this be handled beforehand?

options.A: Clean directly, because cleaning is meant to reduce contamination anyway and no special handling of work-in-process is needed
options.B: As long as a lower concentration of cleaning agent is used, there is no need to specially handle work-in-process or adjust the procedure
options.C: Assess whether cleaning exposes the product or process to risk, and remove or cover the work-in-process before cleaning
options.D: Sample the work-in-process after cleaning is finished to check for contamination, and deal with any problem then

questions.explanation: §4.6.5 requires an assessment of which cleaning procedures would expose the product or process to risk, and removal or covering of work-in-process before cleaning starts. Sampling afterward cannot remedy contamination that has already occurred.

questions.question: What is the focus of what ISO 14644-7 specifies for separative devices (such as isolators, gloveboxes, and mini-environments)?

options.A: Minimum requirements for design, construction, installation, testing, and approval, focusing on the differences from cleanrooms
options.B: The operating details and process conditions of every kind of process
options.C: Replacing the air cleanliness definitions and test methods of ISO 14644-1 and 14644-2
options.D: A complete specification covering fire, safety, and other regulatory matters

questions.explanation: Part 7 specifies minimum requirements for the design, construction, installation, testing, and approval of separative devices, and only for the differences from the cleanrooms described in ISO 14644-4 and 14644-5. It does not specify any particular process, nor does it specifically address fire and safety regulations; the air cleanliness definitions and test methods of Parts 1, 2, and 3 still apply.

questions.question: What is the requirement for hourly leak rate when selecting a transfer device for an isolator?

options.A: As long as the transfer device is fitted with a HEPA filter, its leak rate need not be separately limited
options.B: The leak rate of the transfer device may be higher than that of the isolator, because the transfer takes a very short time and the risk is limited
options.C: The leak rate must be below the particle concentration limit of ISO Class 5 in ISO 14644-1 to be acceptable
options.D: The hourly leak rate must not be greater than that of the separative device it serves

questions.explanation: A transfer device is selected according to the degree of separation required by the application, and its hourly leak rate must not be greater than that of the separative device it serves, otherwise it becomes a weak point in overall integrity. Leak rate and particle cleanliness classification are different measurement concepts.

questions.question: According to ISO 14644-7 Annex E on hourly leak rate testing, which statement is correct?

options.A: Testing is performed only at normal operating pressure (about 250 Pa), and acceptance testing may not use a higher pressure either
options.B: About 250 Pa for checks during operation, and up to 1,000 Pa for acceptance testing
options.C: Both acceptance testing and checks during operation must be uniformly performed at 1,000 Pa
options.D: Leak rate testing is not affected by ambient temperature, so there is no need to let the temperature stabilize before testing

questions.explanation: Leak rate is measured at normal operating pressure (usually about 250 Pa) for checks during operation, while acceptance testing may go up to 1,000 Pa. The device must be at rest before testing; a temperature change of 1 K changes the pressure in a constant volume by 334 Pa, which produces an apparent leak.

questions.question: What is the induction leak mentioned in ISO 14644-7, and under what circumstances is the risk higher?

options.A: Air velocity at an opening causes a pressure drop that induces reverse inflow (Venturi effect); the risk is higher at low pressure differential or when gloves are moved in and out
options.B: Gas permeates outward through the material because the pressure differential is too high; the risk is highest for devices operating at high pressure differential over long periods
options.C: Particles leak into the chamber because of a damaged HEPA filter; the risk is highest during filter replacement work
options.D: Outside air enters because a power interruption prevents the door lock from engaging; the risk is highest during a power failure or backup power changeover

questions.explanation: An induction leak is a reverse flow induced by the pressure reduction that velocity at an opening produces (the Venturi effect). Devices operated at low pressure differential, or relying on positive pressure or airflow to prevent ingress, are more susceptible at moments of volume change such as glove movement in and out.

questions.question: A process requires molecular-level separation (molecular containment), and the team plans to use a glove and sleeve system as the access device. According to ISO 14644-7, how should this be considered?

options.A: A glove and sleeve system can maintain molecular containment as long as the gloves are replaced regularly
options.B: As long as the glove material is chemically compatible, molecular containment is satisfied
options.C: A half-suit guarantees molecular containment better than gloves, so a half-suit should be used instead
options.D: Such flexible film systems are unlikely to maintain molecular containment, and alternative systems should be considered

questions.explanation: Part 7 notes that flexible film systems such as gauntlets, gloves, and half-suits are unlikely to maintain molecular containment, and applications requiring molecular containment should consider alternative systems. A half-suit is also a flexible film system, so it does not solve the problem.
